entities.summary: Joseph Raymond McCarthy was an American politician who served as a Republican U.S. senator from Wisconsin from 1947 until his death in 1957. Beginning in 1950, McCarthy became the most visible public face of a period in the United States in which Cold War tensions fueled fears of widespread communist subversion. He alleged that numerous communists and Soviet spies and sympathizers had infiltrated the United States federal government, universities, film industry, and elsewhere. Ultimately, he was censured by the Senate in 1954 for refusing to cooperate with and abusing members of the committee established to investigate whether or not he should be censured.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: McCarthy's accusations led to the blacklisting of over 5,000 suspected communists, with many losing their jobs and facing social ostracism. His actions also contributed to the Red Scare, a period of intense anti-communist hysteria that lasted for decades.
